methods.name: BRC local neighbor-square lift fixed-gap shortcut
triggers: large v2 of N plus or minus a small distance
known square divisor of N plus or minus d
capabilities: derive m=2a-epsilon*d from any known a^2 dividing N-epsilon*d
reduce the multiplier-Fermat test to squarehood of mt+1 with fixed gap root abs(a-epsilon*d)
discover the unique signed distance in certain bounded power-of-two neighborhoods using one low-bit mask rather than scanning d
prove that absence of the unique start-level distance prevents every higher power-of-two level from reviving a candidate in the same distance window
enumerate all beyond-horizon power-of-two levels on the unique neighbor when all_levels is requested
probe only multipliers beyond an existing bounded horizon
reuse the exact BALANCED quadratic-residue cascade before isqrt
recover a proper factor by gcd when the exact square witness splits N
return immediately to the ordinary exact fallback on a miss
methods.core_law: If N=a^2 t+epsilon*d with epsilon in {+1,-1} and m=2a-epsilon*d, then mN=a^2(mt+1)-(a-epsilon*d)^2. Therefore mt+1=c^2 gives mN=(ac)^2-(a-epsilon*d)^2. For a0=2^k satisfying 2(a0/2)+D<=H<2a0+D and 2D<a0^2, every beyond-H power-of-two candidate with |d|<=D shares the unique signed residue d determined by N mod a0^2. If that residue lies outside D, no higher power-of-two level can revive a candidate. For H=100,D=64 the exact start level is a0=32, so the full radius-64 distance search reduces to one N mod1024 low-bit observation plus at most one v2 chain.
methods.hard_boundary: This remains a specialization of classical multiplier-Fermat/difference-of-squares inside T0_BRC. The local-window compression removes distance-scan overhead but does not increase the mathematical density of square hits. The committed balanced diagnostic has one horizon-extending hit in the 1009..4999-prime cohort and no hits in the larger 10007..50000 or random-24-bit-prime cohorts at H=100,D=64. It must not replace a complete scan, must not trigger open-ended distance/horizon expansion after a miss, and establishes no asymptotic factorization improvement.

methods.name: BRC multiplier square-content scan reduction
capabilities: exact one-shot stripping of every multiplier square factor whose root divides the known BRC ceiling root

methods.core_law: Write m=a^2 d with d squarefree and x=ceil(sqrt(mn)). Under gcd(n,m)=1, g=gcd(a,x) divides the square root y of every successful completion gap y^2=x^2-mn. Dividing m,x,y by g^2,g,g yields the exact immediate ceiling witness at m/g^2, and gcd(x-y,n)=gcd(x/g-y/g,n). After this one-shot normalization gcd(a/g,x/g)=1, so all square content visible in the current ceiling root has been removed.
methods.hard_boundary: Requires an already-known exact ceiling root and declared gcd(n,m)=1; a nontrivial multiplier gcd should be handled as a factor witness before this reduction. Squareful multipliers are not statically discardable: states with gcd(square-content-root,ceiling-root)=1 can be genuine first hits. Common-factor scaling is elementary prior art; no novelty priority, asymptotic factorization speedup, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC fixed-phase root/remainder third-difference transport

methods.core_law: For phase-spaced states (m+8i)N=J_i^2+R_i, let a=J_1-J_0, b=J_2-J_1 and C=3J_2-3J_1+J_0. Then (m+24)N-C^2=R_0-3R_1+3R_2-6b(b-a). On 4m^5>=N, e=J_3-C is the integer third phase difference and satisfies -3<=e<=387. For C>=75078, floor(G/(2C+1)) lies in {e,e+1}; the existing Round-13 1 KiB lower-reciprocal table recovers that floor with at most two increments, and one sign check yields the exact (J_3,R_3).
methods.observer_contract: Retain three labeled phase triples (m_i,J_i,R_i). Roots alone, Boolean support, or an unlabeled aggregate are inadequate because the exact residual and future completion-gap observer depend on the individual remainders and phase order.
methods.hard_boundary: Exact integer transport only on the already-certified odd-N order-one deep tail and fixed mod-8 representative phases. The finite performance crossover is runtime-dependent; direct division remains appropriate for smaller operands. This does not reduce the multiplier horizon, change Lehman/Hart factorization complexity, imply RSA practicality, or create a new top-level BRC family.

methods.name: BRC error linearization / Pell-Pade tail transport

methods.core_law: For E_K=sqrt(1+x)-1-P_K, derivatives above order K satisfy (1+x)E_K^(n+1)/E_K^n=1/2-n, while ordinary BRC correction gaps satisfy G_q=G_0-q(2a+q). The diagonal Pade/Pell approximant obtained from (1+sqrt(1+x))^(2n+1)=P_n+sqrt(1+x)Q_n yields homogenized integers A_n,B_n with (m+h)B_n^2-mA_n^2=h^(2n+1). methods.hard_boundary: Classical Pade/Pell approximation is prior art. The current contribution is exact BRC composition, certification, and error-linearization bookkeeping. The Python reference path is substantially faster than the previous high-order Taylor table-free tail but still slower than direct optimized isqrt on isolated steps. No asymptotic factorization speedup, RSA-practicality, optimal multiplier order, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC prioritized direct multiplier jump / 2-adic irredundant scan
capabilities: exact elimination of odd-N multipliers m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 as impossible difference-of-squares targets
exact reduction of every successful immediate witness at m congruent 4 mod 8 to the smaller multiplier m/4 with the same gcd factor
scan-complete odd-N static multiplier representative residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8

direct exact BRC transport from the retained m=1 root/remainder state to arbitrary target m<=100
proved at-most-11 odd-basin corrections for direct jumps
methods.core_law: For odd N, m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 is impossible as a difference of squares. If 4 divides m and an immediate ceiling-square witness has even ceiling root x, then its gap root is even and dividing x,y,m by 2,2,4 gives the same immediate witness and gcd factor at m/4; this may be repeated using the halved ceiling root. The static special case m=4*l with l odd therefore makes every 4 mod 8 multiplier redundant and leaves residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8 scan-complete. For target t<=100 the retained m=1 BRC state reaches t exactly with at most 11 odd-basin corrections.
methods.hard_boundary: Difference-of-squares feasibility, static scan irredundancy, and state-dependent gap-test irredundancy are distinct. The static/dynamic 2-adic reductions and direct jump are exact; the same-parity factor-pair ranking is only a finite empirically useful heuristic and is not claimed optimal. Retained 0 mod 8 states with odd ceiling root can be genuine first hits, so that class cannot be uniformly deleted. Multiplier-Fermat/Hart/Lehman remains classical prior art. No global novelty priority, asymptotic factorization speedup, theorem about semiprime ratio distributions, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.core_law: With gamma_m=sqrt((m+1)/m)-1, choose B so J_m<2^(B-1), C_m=floor(2^B gamma_m), d0=floor(C_m J_m/2^B). Then J_(m+1)-(J_m+d0) is in {0,1,2}. The provisional remainder is R_m+N-d0(2J_m+d0); subtracting successive odd basin widths at most twice yields exactly R_(m+1).
methods.hard_boundary: Finite exact integer multiplier scan only; checked-in static performance fast path N<=4096 bits and m<=100. No asymptotic factorization speedup, no novelty claim for multiplier-Fermat/Lehman square-gap factoring, no recovery after erasing R_m, and no Foundation promotion.

methods.name: BRC multiplier x vertical residue-wheel / lazy exact gap calculus

methods.core_law: For fixed m,N and x_0=ceil(sqrt(mN)), D_t=(x_0+t)^2-mN is periodic modulo M as a function of t mod M. Therefore every exact square hit lies in W_M={r:(x_0+r)^2-mN is a quadratic residue mod M}. Enumerating only translated copies of W_M is observer-safe for squarehood rejection; exact D_t can be reconstructed as D_0+t(2x_0+t) only after surviving all declared modular observers.
methods.hard_boundary: Vertical Fermat search, additive gap recurrence, congruence stepping, quadratic-residue sieving, and Lehman/Hart factoring are classical prior art. The adaptive 1008/20160 wheel threshold is a finite Python benchmark policy, not a theorem. Timing gains inside a fixed search rectangle do not reduce the classical rectangle size or imply an asymptotic factoring improvement. No Foundation promotion is made.

methods.name: BRC square-gap quadratic-residue prefilter
capabilities: checked-in exact packed quadratic-residue tables for moduli 4032 and 20160
deterministic cached fallback table generation for arbitrary positive moduli
zero-false-negative rejection of impossible square gaps

typed separation of BRC next-square addition cost from ceiling-square Fermat completion cost

methods.core_law: If an integer value is a square then its residue modulo M belongs to the precomputed quadratic-residue table Q_M. Therefore Q_M[value mod M]=0 safely rejects squarehood before exact isqrt confirmation. For M=4032 the table has 192 live residue classes out of 4032 (1/21) and a 504-byte raw payload; for M=20160 it has 576 live classes out of 20160 (1/35) and a 2520-byte raw payload.
methods.hard_boundary: Quadratic-residue filtering, Fermat difference of squares, and Lehman-style multiplier use are classical prior art. Passing the residue filter is not a square certificate. Rejection percentage is not runtime speedup: on the checked small-integer semiprime sample direct Python isqrt was faster, while deterministic larger-integer timing showed the table becomes useful; full ceiling-gap pipeline gains were only about 1.2-1.4x in the tested big-integer ranges because ceil(sqrt(mN)) remains on the critical path. Timings are environment-dependent diagnostics, not complexity theorems. Coarse BRC basin support/Pell resonance remains unpromoted as a selector.
